statusDefinitions.planned: Design stage; must not be a production dependency.
statusDefinitions.pilot: Controlled validation stage with protected production writes.
statusDefinitions.deprecated: Migration or read-only stage with a documented replacement.
statusDefinitions.archived: Retained in Git history or releases and not deployed as an active entry point.

applications.name: NEXUS Home
applications.purpose: Identify the master or delegated user, record login and logout through the deployed authentication service, show the fixed ONEAPP ownership Footer, and launch independent work apps without gating their local execution or depending on the company service.
coreCapabilities: per-user home-card and global-tab visibility projection without access gating
fixed ownership Footer without server or identity dependencies
applications.offlinePolicy: A cached unexpired home session and the fixed ownership Footer remain visible while authentication verification is delayed; company-service failure does not affect home, and work apps do not load the login runtime or wait for the authentication service.

applications.name: NEXUS User Administration
applications.purpose: Let only OWNER_MASTER create delegated users, update display names and non-authoritative app visibility, suspend or restore use, reissue one-time activation codes, and review minimal immutable audit events without deletion, capability, service, or approval controls.
applications.offlinePolicy: Authentication-service failure disables only administration; it does not redirect or block independent work-app entry and local work.

applications.name: NEXUS Company Profile
applications.purpose: Let only OWNER_MASTER users with admin.company read and revise the server-authoritative company profile while preserving revision conflicts and audit writes.
applications.offlinePolicy: Server failure leaves the last NEXUS home Snapshot unchanged and is never converted into an empty company record.

applications.name: MerchOps
applications.purpose: Consume an immutable owner-issued Product Snapshot, prepare pricing, promotion, and Excel-based product-information work, explicitly register reviewed missing products through the product-owner command, and apply reviewed F7 field patches through the same versioned owner boundary.
applications.offlinePolicy: Render with the last readable Product Snapshot and preserve current work locally. Module or owner-repository unavailability disables command/request writes without blocking F8, F9, or local work recovery.

applications.name: DataOps
applications.purpose: Analyze purchase, sales, inventory, stock ledger, cost, and performance information, including administrator-reviewed out-of-list inventory products from the confirmed local master.

applications.name: Smart Parser
applications.purpose: Parse external documents locally into immutable analysis results, match against Product Snapshots, submit reviewed product proposals as PENDING owner requests, and own supplier exclusions plus explicit atomic stop/resume commands.

applications.name: Export Center
applications.purpose: Review the existing MerchOps F9 draft and generate Excel or image output without changing product master, history, or revision.
applications.offlinePolicy: Preserve and render the existing draft when Product Snapshot is EMPTY, ERROR, unavailable, or stale. Output remains available from draft values and never writes product master or history.

applications.name: Settings
applications.purpose: Own mappings, pricing policies, columns, table views, cloud URL, and validated atomic settings backup and recovery while routing product and SmartParser operations to their owner apps.
applications.offlinePolicy: Render and edit locally owned configuration without waiting for cloud or another app. Cloud recovery validates the complete allowlist, captures a pre-image, rolls back on failure, and preserves unknown external fields.

applications.name: 상품관리
applications.purpose: Own the official product-reference management boundary on the existing MerchOpsDB contract, provide immutable read snapshots, receive idempotent change requests for review, and retain controlled administrator-reviewed master writes.

applications.name: 거래처관리
applications.purpose: Own and manage customer reference data, aliases, external-code mappings, revisions, local history, Excel upserts, snapshots, and a read-only consumer snapshot without requiring authentication or cloud availability.
applications.offlinePolicy: Render, search, edit, import, back up, and restore customer data from the app-owned IndexedDB without waiting for login, cloud, another app, or an external CDN.

applications.name: Item Manager
applications.purpose: Provide category-based product lookup and controlled product-management writes.

applications.name: History Viewer
applications.purpose: Read immutable local or cloud product-change history, inspect price trends, and export the exact current view without modifying the history repository.
applications.offlinePolicy: Render local history independently, distinguish READY, EMPTY, ERROR, and NOT_AVAILABLE, and keep cloud results in memory only. Product Snapshot or cloud failure never becomes a successful empty result.

applications.name: ONEAPP Core Engine
applications.purpose: Provide common storage, pricing, history, export, cloud, and master-data utilities.
applications.integrationNote: Settings explicitly loads this library. Other production pages still contain overlapping local implementations and require compatibility validation before consolidation.

applications.name: ORDER Q
applications.purpose: Manage the shipment workflow from customer order through available inventory, purchasing, staged shipment completion, and reviewed outbound workbooks.

applications.name: ORDER Q vNext
applications.purpose: Provide manual and text order intake, source-preserving historical collection, order-to-sales fulfillment evidence, and the owner boundary for official purchase/sale commands, documents, revisions, inventory or pending effects, base AR/AP effects, the read-only unresolved-product review model and impact preview, and the official local sync queue without changing the existing OrderOps compatibility route.

applications.name: SmartInput
applications.purpose: Create order, purchase, sale, and estimate work through one automatically updated local recovery state while consuming owner-issued product and customer Snapshots and requesting official purchase/sale changes through the ORDER Q owner command boundary, without direct writes to ORDER Q raw stores.
coreCapabilities: per-voucher field registry and minimal visible field settings
revisioned purchase and sale official command-adapter requests to the ORDER Q owner boundary

dependencyMode.officialVoucherRemoteSync: BACKGROUND_SYNC through ONEAPP_ORDERQ_OFFICIAL_SYNC_V1; unsupported or unavailable server keeps WAITING_SERVER_CONTRACT without blocking local finalize

applications.offlinePolicy: Render the application and preserve the latest local work state and work-table edits without waiting for authentication, server, reference data, or optional Excel, OCR, and speech dependencies.

applications.name: NEXUS Auth Gateway Transport
applications.purpose: Own the deployed NEXUS_AUTH_V2 user, Session, visibility, minimal audit, and retained company/Gateway contracts while preserving the official deployment ID and versioned rollback.

applications.name: ONEAPP Cloud Sync
applications.purpose: Back up and restore product master, history, shared configuration, the finalized DataOps inventory snapshot, explicitly saved Shipping purchase-plan revisions, token-protected ORDER Q vNext incremental records and company-partitioned official voucher commands, and the revisioned NEXUS company profile boundary.

sharedDataContracts.writerPolicy: The server requires a current Session, OWNER_MASTER/admin.company, an app-scoped Gateway context, and expectedRevision for every profile write.

resources.homeDependency: NONE; nexus/index.html renders a fixed ownership Footer without company reads
resources.upstreamDeploymentPolicy: Preserve the existing ONEAPP Apps Script deployment ID; restore the company boundary without running migration; retain upstream v44 as the immediate rollback version.

sharedDataContracts.writerPolicy: Only customer-master receives requests into its appMeta-owned additive inbox. Receipt remains PENDING and never applies customer master data automatically.
ORDER Q owns voucher documents and lines. SmartInput and the query page consume a date-scoped read-only Snapshot and never write through this adapter.
Only the explicit full-refresh action stages all six owner snapshots and atomically activates a validated immutable generation. Partial failure keeps the previous active generation.
The import plan copies an immutable source voucher snapshot into the selected target draft and never updates the source voucher or source line.

ORDER Q owns the official command gateway and repository. SmartInput is a command-adapter consumer and must not write ORDER Q raw stores. The current repository uses company partitioning, optimistic revision, idempotent command IDs, and one local IndexedDB finalize transaction for document and lines, command receipt, voucher revision, matched inventory movement or unresolved pending effect, the currently validated partner's base payable/receivable entry, unresolved-product identity, and the official syncQueue row. V2 retains that atomic unit while creating base AR/AP only for an exact company-scoped Customer Snapshot match and omitting AR/AP, without blocking the voucher or inventory path, when the customer is absent or unmatched.
sharedDataContracts.consumerBoundary: SmartInput purchase and sale UI handlers call their separate Finalize Services. The existing purchase/sale builders then call the ORDER Q official command Adapter, which delegates through OfficialCommandGateway to OfficialVoucherRepository. SmartInput production modules have no direct repository import. Phase 6C rematch and Phase 7A owner-only correction/cancel build/commit also pass through the same boundary. Phase 7A has no product UI consumer or entry point; any future product connection is subject to UI Gate U2.
sharedDataContracts.userProductIdentity: companyId + ERP productCode string; preserve leading zeroes and do not expose a new NXP identifier
sharedDataContracts.compatibilityProductIdentity: productId remains a non-visible Product Snapshot technical key for the current inventory, checkpoint, rematch, and sync stores
sharedDataContracts.migrationPolicy: No V1 official-voucher, Draft, or test-data migration. Continue additively inside SmartInput DB v5 and ORDER Q DB v7 without deleting or initializing existing stores or records.

sharedDataContracts.writerPolicy: Only the ORDER Q shopping-order command Adapter delegates to the owner Repository. The Repository reads actual ORDER Q orders and orderItems, recomputes the company/customer/delivery-date/warehouse/item-multiset signature and actual count inside each candidate's existing DB v7 transaction, and writes only the next surplus order with its items, creation event and local queue rows. Duplicate and review-required candidates write nothing; a failed candidate transaction does not roll back a different candidate.
sharedDataContracts.identityPolicy: The signature uses company, owner-resolved customer, delivery date, owner-resolved shipment warehouse, and a duplicate-preserving item multiset of product identity, specification, unit, quantity, unit price and amount. A candidate is scorable and writable only when customerId, warehouseId and every item productId plus its stored code and name are resolved; otherwise that candidate is REVIEW_REQUIRED with isDuplicate=null and zero writes. Source order status, group, filename, upload time, absolute row number, memo, address and phone remain immutable evidence but do not change isDuplicate. Existing manual ORDER Q orders count when the same actual signature can be derived; a potentially matching legacy bundle with incomplete owner identity fails closed as EXISTING_LEDGER_BUNDLE_INVALID.
sharedDataContracts.occurrencePolicy: For source occurrence n and actual-ledger count m, isDuplicate is n <= m and the surplus is max(0,n-m). The sourceMessageKey is an internal signature-plus-occurrence idempotency key, never a fabricated external order number. Each write transaction rechecks m before insertion and resolves a matching unique-key race to the existing order.
sharedDataContracts.boundaryPolicy: The fixed 17-column shopping source has no order number. Group is not an order identifier. A changed company/customer/delivery-date/warehouse scope or an explicit upstream source boundary starts a candidate; non-contiguous same-customer runs stay separate. Repeated adjacent order-content sequences inside one otherwise unbounded customer run fail closed as AMBIGUOUS_SOURCE_ORDER_BOUNDARY.
sharedDataContracts.activationPolicy: Owner core and Adapter only. SmartInput product UI and upload flow are not connected in this phase. This is local actual-ledger idempotency and does not claim multi-device global duplicate prevention.
sharedDataContracts.migrationPolicy: Reuse oneapp-orderq-pre-m1-v6 DB version 7 and the existing orders, orderItems, orderEvents, syncQueue and meta Stores plus the existing unique orders.bySourceMessageKey index. No DB version, Store, key, index, migration, reset or existing record rewrite is introduced.
sharedDataContracts.rollback: Revert the Phase 1 core, Adapter, Repository, manifest, architecture, report and tests as one commit. This removes future shopping-order calls without deleting or rewriting any ORDER Q DB v7 data; orders already created through an explicitly invoked owner command remain ordinary auditable ORDER Q facts.

sharedDataContracts.readerPolicy: Company scope is mandatory. Only the ORDER Q owner Repository opens the existing official stores and composes unresolved records, pending effects, confirmed documents, lines, Revisions, and stocktake checkpoints. Same-effect review evidence is deduplicated only after shared link fields are reconciled; conflicts remain REVIEW_REQUIRED. A cross-company point-get target contributes only a mismatch issue and none of its payload. EMPTY and ERROR remain distinct; an owner read failure is never represented as zero rows.
sharedDataContracts.candidatePolicy: The current Product Snapshot is reference-only. An outer-trimmed exact source-string code may be marked as an exact candidate only when unique under the Product owner company rule. Leading-zero, case, character-width, and internal-space variants remain distinct. Name candidates are reference-only and never auto-confirmed.
sharedDataContracts.writePolicy: Read model and rematch impact preview only. No rematch command, inventory write, Product or Customer write, UI execution, schema migration, or Store creation is permitted.
sharedDataContracts.rollback: Phase 6B rollback removes orderops/unresolved-review-ui.js, the orderops/list.html result-state branch, and the orderops consumer registration. The Phase 6A owner read assets and existing ORDER Q DB v7 data remain untouched; a full Phase 6A rollback may then remove those owner assets and this contract registration separately.

sharedDataContracts.writerPolicy: Only the ORDER Q OfficialCommandAdapter to OfficialCommandGateway to OfficialVoucherRepository path may commit a rematch. The former raw local Repository entry point fails closed. A command requires explicit non-automatic user selection, current company and Product Snapshot identity, complete expected document/line/Revision/pending-effect links, actor, occurredAt, judgedAt, commandId and idempotencyKey. Before opening a write transaction, a readonly source preflight recalculates warehouse, factor-1 actual quantity, purchase/sale sign, calendar-valid business date and only source-trusted business time from the confirmed document, active confirmed line and immutable Revision, and reconciles both pending and review evidence to the same original command. The Repository repeats that defense and the Phase 5 pure stocktake classifier inside one DB v7 transaction before updating resolution/effects and adding inventory or absorption effects, one audit Revision, one receipt and one local queue row. Confirmed document/line Snapshots are immutable.
sharedDataContracts.candidatePolicy: The selected Product Snapshot row must be active, unique by its hidden productId in the current company scope, and exactly equal on product code, name, specification and unit. Product name or similarity never auto-confirms; automaticConfirmation must be false.
sharedDataContracts.stocktakePolicy: Proven-after or no-checkpoint effects apply their preserved signed quantity. Before-checkpoint and same-day-unproven effects require a decision for every row. Zero quantity always keeps effectStatus ZERO_EFFECT; its independent stocktakeEffectStatus is blank for normal, ABSORBED_BY_CHECKPOINT for included, or APPLIED_AS_LATE_ADJUSTMENT for not included. Included has stock delta zero and officialInventoryApplied false; normal and not included remain true, with not included creating exactly one deterministic movement. Both statuses are retained in resolved pending effects and the audit Revision. The legacy RESOLVED_WITHOUT_MOVEMENT_AFTER_STOCKTAKE result is forbidden in this command.
sharedDataContracts.activationPolicy: Default OFF. Phase 6C adds no product UI consumer and does not enable Pilot, production, or Cloud Push/Pull. OFFICIAL_INVENTORY_REMATCH_COMMAND queue rows remain WAITING_SERVER_CONTRACT outside the Cloud entity allowlist.
sharedDataContracts.migrationPolicy: Reuse existing oneapp-orderq-pre-m1-v6 DB version 7 Stores and indexes. No Store, schema migration, data initialization, deletion, or rewrite of confirmed source Snapshots.
sharedDataContracts.rollback: Revert the Phase 6C command/core/Gateway/Repository and contract/test changes as one commit. This disables future 6C calls without deleting existing DB v7 rows; any committed rematch is an auditable business fact and must not be erased by rollback. The Phase 6A read model and Phase 6B read-only UI remain available.

sharedDataContracts.writerPolicy: CORRECT and CANCEL may be committed only through OfficialCommandAdapter to OfficialCommandGateway to OfficialVoucherRepository. The command carries company, voucher kind, document ID, expected current Revision, action, actor, zoned occurredAt, deterministic commandId=idempotencyKey, payload digest, a hash-verified complete current Head target and the complete replacement Snapshot for CORRECT. The Repository performs a readonly preflight and repeats document, ACTIVE/CONFIRMED lines, latest immutable Revision hashes, current effect links, command receipt scope, company, kind and expected Revision checks in the one readwrite transaction. It advances only the current projection to a new immutable Revision and never changes an older Revision or Snapshot.
sharedDataContracts.referencePolicy: Unchanged confirmation-time product and partner identity/Snapshot evidence remains usable even if the current master row was deleted. Each newly added or changed MATCHED product is validated against the current Product owner Snapshot for company-scoped exact unique ERP code, productId, code, name, specification, unit and revision. Each changed partner resolution is validated against the current Customer owner Snapshot; a changed MATCHED partner is then rejected because Phase 7A cannot create its required AR/AP effect.
sharedDataContracts.headIntegrityPolicy: Initial POST businessSnapshot and Phase 7A full afterSnapshot formats are explicit. Every field stored by the applicable Snapshot format is reconciled with the current document and ACTIVE/CONFIRMED line projection, including business and identity values and command/Revision links. status and businessStatus must both independently be CONFIRMED.
sharedDataContracts.inventoryPolicy: CORRECT records separately traceable reversal rows for current effective inventory effects and revised application rows, or supersedes/creates pending unresolved effects. Purchase is +quantity, sale is -quantity; positive, zero and negative quantities and factor 1 are preserved. Matched/unmatched transitions, product, warehouse and business-date changes, and Phase 6C-rematched lines use the same plan. CANCEL keeps document and lines, creates a CANCELLED Revision and reverses only effects that were actually applied; an absorbed effect produces an auditable zero reversal. ZERO_EFFECT, stocktakeEffectStatus and REVERSED remain independent audit meanings.
sharedDataContracts.sourceEffectIntegrityPolicy: A current effective movement is eligible for reversal only after productId/code, warehouse, businessDate/effectiveAt, source document Revision and hashed Revision lineage, commandId, movement/effect role/status, factor, signedQuantity and originalSignedQuantity are reconciled to the source document and line. Normal, absorbed, late adjustment, revision-after and Phase 6C rematch shapes are validated explicitly; an equal aggregate quantity cannot authorize a mismatched movement.
sharedDataContracts.unresolvedLifecyclePolicy: The unresolved top-level state is derived from all active review links after each supersede/cancel. No active link yields NO_ACTIVE_REVIEW while preserving closed audit links and excluding the record from the Phase 6B unresolved list. An already MATCHED unresolved identity is never downgraded or cleared; reuse for a new pending effect fails closed with full transaction rollback.
sharedDataContracts.stocktakePolicy: Every inventory delta row reuses the Phase 5 evaluateStocktakeCheckpointConflictV2 classifier at its own original businessDate. Before-checkpoint and same-day-unproven rows require one current included/not-included decision. No Repository write starts until all row decisions exist and are rechecked; cancel before commit returns officialWrites 0.
sharedDataContracts.partnerEffectPolicy: Phase 7A creates, changes, deletes or reverses no payable or receivable entry. If the current document has any linked base payable/receivable entry, correction and cancellation fail closed with ORDERQ_OFFICIAL_REVISION_ARAP_EFFECT_UNSUPPORTED. AR/AP closing, adjustment, tax invoice and offset policy remain follow-up scope.
sharedDataContracts.activationPolicy: CORRECT_PURCHASE, CANCEL_PURCHASE, CORRECT_SALE and CANCEL_SALE gates are independent and default OFF. No product UI is connected. OFFICIAL_VOUCHER_REVISION_COMMAND queue rows stay WAITING_SERVER_CONTRACT and are outside the current official Cloud allowlist; Pilot, production and Cloud Push/Pull are not activated.
sharedDataContracts.migrationPolicy: Reuse oneapp-orderq-pre-m1-v6 DB version 7 and its existing Stores and indexes. No Store, DB version, schema migration, data initialization or deletion is introduced.
sharedDataContracts.rollback: Revert the Phase 7A single commit. This removes future owner correction/cancel entry points and gates without changing DB v7 or Phase 0-6C. Any explicitly committed Revision/effect rows are immutable audit facts and are not deleted automatically; the default-off gates prevent new calls.

sharedDataContracts.writerPolicy: Local purchase and sale finalize remains LOCAL_OPERATION. Background sync stores immutable command payloads by company, applies command-id idempotency and voucher-revision optimistic locking, and never overwrites a conflicting local voucher or active SmartInput draft.
sharedDataContracts.activationPolicy: Excluded from the SmartInput official-voucher and inventory V2 implementation scope until separate server deployment, company-isolation, multi-device, and production-activation validation is approved.

sharedDataContracts.purpose: Identify and retry sale-resume work after the related DataOps inventory snapshot has already finalized successfully.
sharedDataContracts.rollback: Reverting the feature stops new records; unresolved records are retained for manual sale-status review and must not trigger another inventory closing. Successfully resumed records are removed after verified master/history commit.

sharedDataContracts.writerPolicy: master-lookup is the official owner. SmartParser reads immutable Product Snapshots and submits product proposals only through PENDING owner requests; its page has no raw product writer. The sole SmartParser exception is the versioned stop-management command adapter, limited to explicit STOP/RESUME/UPDATE_METADATA with expected Snapshot/revision and atomic sale-status/linked-state/history/mirror/notification handling. MerchOps may change existing product fields only through its reviewed F7 command and may create operator-selected missing products only through MERCHOPS_PRODUCT_REGISTRATION_V1; quantity and business date remain work values. Legacy globals and all other workflows fail closed with OWNER_ROUTED.
Only master-lookup receives requests into the existing owner KV store. Receipt remains PENDING and never applies product master data automatically.

Pure local create/normalize/validate/clone/freeze contract. It stores no product master, history, stop state, server queue, raw source document, or credentials. Product proposals are submitted separately through the product owner PENDING request adapter.
master-lookup owns the repository. History Viewer and MerchOps consume immutable snapshots; append is allowed only inside approved owner commands that atomically verify product writes and history.

Settings writes only its versioned allowlist. JSON and cloud recovery validate all values before apply, capture a pre-image, rollback and verify on failure, preserve unknown cloud fields, and exclude product, history, pending, stop, and product-status live data.

sharedDataContracts.consumerPolicy: Export Center reads and reviews the existing draft shape without changing it. Optional sidecar metadata binds the draft fingerprint to the Product Snapshot version for exact stale detection; legacy drafts use content comparison.
MerchOps reads the parser dictionary for work interpretation only and never writes, merges, resets, restores, or cloud-synchronizes it.

sharedDataContracts.writerPolicy: SmartParser owns explicit general STOP/RESUME/UPDATE_METADATA only through its versioned command adapter, with normalized unique codes, expected Product Snapshot/revision, operation idempotency, atomic product sale status, stopped list, pending status, actual history, local mirrors and notifications, plus stale-safe rollback. Analysis results and PENDING product requests never invoke this command automatically. DataOps retains its existing post-close resume-only masterAddUpdate.js boundary.

sharedDataContracts.consumerPolicy: MerchOps reads the owner value into memory and never seeds, persists, resets, restores, or cloud-synchronizes it.
MerchOps reads mappings and links into work memory and does not persist owner configuration.
MerchOps consumes saved views read-only. Active work selection is stored only in merchops-work-view-state.
MerchOps displays and routes this setting but performs no full backup, restore, seed, or write.

sharedDataContracts.writerPolicy: Additive MerchOps-only current-work selection. It must not replace or mutate Settings-owned table-view configuration.

changeRules.policy: Function keys are application-owned. The same key must not be assumed to have the same business meaning across applications.

plannedApplications.name: Trend Report
plannedApplications.purpose: Turn MerchOps and DataOps results into decision-support insights after the core applications mature.
validation: Every reported metric identifies its source and period.
Results reconcile with the source application totals.
The report cannot mutate production data.
plannedApplications.rollback: Remove pilot navigation and retain generated reports only as non-authoritative artifacts.

plannedApplications.name: Image Generator
plannedApplications.purpose: Create offline-sales images and print materials for market-price changes and promotional products.
plannedApplications.workflowIntent: MerchOps F9 review leads to a downstream F10 print action after the output workflow is approved.
validation: Printed values match the approved review payload.
Preview and print layouts remain legible at the target paper size.
Image generation cannot mutate product master data.
plannedApplications.rollback: Disable the pilot output entry and continue using existing Excel or manual print output.
resumeAfter: MerchOps Export Center workflow is stable.
Output and print validation rules are approved.

recoveryPolicy.sourceOfTruth: Git history and the main branch
recoveryPolicy.optionalPreviewPolicy: Keep at most one explicitly named preview or stable entry point per operational need, with an owner and verification date.

merchops.F7: Apply current work to the MerchOps master after atomic storage and history verification.
merchops.F8: Create the Excel output from current work without changing the master.
merchops.F9: Open Export Center for review and downstream output.

export-center.F9: Generate the reviewed Excel output without writing product master, history, revision, or sync triggers.
export-center.F10: Generate the existing temporary image-output payload without changing product master.

dataops.F6: Open one out-of-list product search row below the selected inventory row using the confirmed local master.
dataops.F9: Create the combined workbook, finalize the DataOps inventory snapshot, then independently resume stopped master products with positive counted inventory.

orderops.F3: Focus the integrated search field and keep the text caret ready for immediate input.
orderops.F7: Print the current visible OrderOps tab, filters, rows, column visibility, and column order on A4 portrait.
orderops.F8: Create the complete integrated OrderOps workbook independently of current screen filters, hidden columns, or column order.
